headlines.title: 49ers vs. Rams live updates: NFC West rivals clash in historic Australia game
headlines.description: What to Know Programming note: NBC Sports Bay Area and NBC Bay Area will provide complete coverage of the 49ers’ season opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, on Thursday, Sept. 10. First, tune in to NBC Sports Bay Area at 4:30 p.m. PT for “49ers Pregame Live.” Then, switch over to NBC Bay Area or Netflix at 5:30 p.m. PT for the game broadcast. As soon as the game ends, flip back to NBC Sports Bay Area for “49ers Postgame Live.” The San Francisco 49ers begin their 2026 NFL season down under, facing off against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1 on Thursday night at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia. The game is a historic one for both teams and for the NFL, which is hosting an international regular-season contest in Melbourne, Australia, for the first time. San Francisco and Los Angeles took entirely different approaches when traveling to Australia, with the 49ers arriving one week ahead of the game and the Rams touching down in the country about 24 hours before kickoff. Several 49ers stars are returning to the field Thursday after season-ending injuries in 2025, including Nick Bosa (ACL), George Kittle (Achilles) and Fred Warner (ankle), while the Rams will have new acquisition Myles Garrett on the field — but not the un-retired Aaron Donald. After defensive tackle Alfred Collins sustained a season-ending knee injury during practice this week, the 49ers elevated defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo and wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge from the practice squad to face the Rams. NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco listed his five 49ers players to watch in Thursday night’s prime-time battle between the two NFC West rivals. Follow this live blog for the latest score updates, game highlights, news and analysis from Melbourne Cricket Ground in East Melbourne:
headlines.source: Angelina Martin, Ali Thanawalla, Nick Avila, Will Simonds, Matt Maiocco and Jennifer Lee Chan

headlines.title: How to watch 49ers vs. Rams NFL season opener in Australia on NBC Bay Area
headlines.description: The 49ers and Los Angeles Rams have descended upon Melbourne for the first-ever NFL game in Australia. The NFC West rivals begin their respective 2026 NFL seasons at 5:35 p.m. PT on Thursday, Sept. 10, at Melbourne Cricket Ground, which holds over 100,000 spectators. But if you didn’t make the trek to Melbourne, don’t worry. NBC Bay Area and NBC Sports Bay Area have you covered. Coverage begins at 4:30 p.m. with an NBC Bay Area special anchored in studio by Janelle Wang and Raj Mathai, with live reports from Australia from sports reporter Anthony Flores. NBC Bay Area will televise Netflix’s programming of the game beginning at 5 p.m. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:35 p.m. The matchup will make history as the NFL’s first regular season game played in Australia. Immediately following the game, NBC Bay Area will air Sports Sunday presented by Xfinity, featuring reaction and analysis from the 49ers’ season opener. NBC Sports Bay Area will also have you covered with “49ers Pregame Live” and “49ers Postgame Live,” featuring comprehensive reaction and analysis from the team, including Matt Maiocco reporting from Melbourne. Don’t miss a minute of the 49ers’ season-opener coverage across NBC Bay Area and NBC Sports Bay Area. headlines.title: Woman arrested after viral video shows hate-motivated incident in San Jose
headlines.description: The woman at the center of a viral video where she appears to approach a father and his child to make discriminatory remarks was arrested, San Jose police said on Friday. Police said the woman was arrested and booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of stalking, hate crimes and in connection with other charges. Police said officers responded to a report of a hate-motivated incident in the 6400 block of Aspen Creek on Sunday. According to authorities, the suspect approached a father and his child in her vehicle multiple times and made discriminatory remarks at them. San Jose police said Automated License Plate Reader cameras were used to identify the associated vehicle and suspect. Officials said it was also discovered the suspect was responsible for various other incidents in San Jose, including an incident at a high school located in South San Jose on Wednesday. Those incidents led San Jose Unified to send out an alert to its community on Thursday, warning them of the woman and stating she has harassed members of the community, including recording videos and posting them on social media. “We want to make you aware of a situation affecting several of our school communities. We have received reports of an individual harassing members of our community, including recording videos and taking photographs, and posting content on social media,” the district wrote. San Jose police said the investigation is active and ongoing and asks anyone with information on these cases to contact SJPD Assaults Unit Detectives at 408-277-4161.

headlines.title: Lanes reopen on I-580 in San Leandro following SWAT activity
headlines.description: Two people are in custody following a standoff that shut down a portion of Interstate 580 in San Leandro, the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office said. The incident was first reported at 11:25 a.m. Thursday when a deputy tried to stop a Ford Mustang for a traffic violation. Authorities said the driver failed to yield and deputies did not pursue out of an abundance of caution and concern for public safety. The suspect vehicle was later located through license plate reader technology and the sheriff’s office deployed a drone to follow. Authorities said the Mustang was later seen driving the wrong way on eastbound I-580 and crashed with another vehicle before continuing to drive away. California Highway Patrol officers in the area also attempted to stop the Mustang, which continued to drive away before the vehicle was disabled and stopped. The sheriff’s office said both occupants of the car refused to come out of the vehicle, prompting a freeway shutdown and standoff. SWAT vehicles also responded to the incident just east of the Benedict Drive offramp. “The passenger eventually exited and surrendered. The driver continued to refuse commands. A chemical irritant was deployed to gain the driver’s compliance, and the driver subsequently exited the vehicle and was taken into custody,” the sheriff’s office said. Both the driver and passenger were taken to a hospital for non-life threatening injuries, officials said, adding the driver of the other vehicle the Mustang crashed into was also transported to a nearby hospital and treated for non-life-threatening injuries. headlines.title: Anthropic says it blocked misuse of its AI that could have supported biological weapons
headlines.description: Anthropic said Thursday it has blocked efforts by bad actors to use its artificial intelligence models for malicious activity such as cyberattacks, surveillance, and research that could have led to biological weapons. As AI models grow more powerful, elaborate cyberattacks no longer require sophisticated skills and even lone individuals can create threats that would not have been possible even a year ago, Anthropic said. The company said it has added stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict biological research that could also be used to make weapons. “The cases we share here aren’t typical misuse, but rather examples of the most notable and novel threat activity we’ve identified to date,” Anthropic said in its third report since March 2025 describing AI misuse. The report includes snippets of the malicious code and AI prompts Anthropic said it found, and urges governments and AI competitors to identify and prevent similar abuse. “We’re publishing this work because we believe we have a responsibility to disclose malicious misuse of our services. As models become increasingly capable, their risks will increase, unless AI developers and society’s defenders act to make them safer,” the company said. The lengthy report by the AI startup, which is planning an initial public offering this fall, was published two days after one of its researchers announced he’s resigning over concerns that Anthropic and its competitors are not acting responsibly in AI development. He echoed concerns raised inside and outside of the industry about the technology’s potential to elude human control. Claude was asked to support making a virus more harmful Between December 2025 and August 2026, researchers at Anthropic found misuse by actors ranging from spyware vendors and “politically motivated individuals” to state-sponsored groups spreading propaganda. Among the findings in the company’s report are unnamed actors attempting to use its models for research that could have led to biological weapons. In one instance, Anthropic said its systems blocked a request for Claude’s assistance in authoring a grant application for scientific funding. “The work discussed in the application involved gain-of-function research (that is, research that genetically alters an organism to create a new or enhanced biological property) on the chikungunya virus. This gain of function research was aimed at the virus’ transmissibility and immune evasion properties,” the report said. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne virus that causes debilitating symptoms such as severe pain and fever. The request involved a grant proposal for research seeking to enhance mutations to make the virus progressively more harmful. While such research could “certainly” be used to develop better vaccines and treatments, Anthropic said, “it could also be used to make the pathogen more dangerous.” Artificial intelligence Sep 9 Artificial intelligence Jul 31 Anthropic says it can’t claim its models do no harm None of the cases Anthropic included in its report were found to be using its newer, more powerful Claude Fable or Mythos-class models, with the exception of one illicit distillation case that Anthropic described as “an industrial-scale, covert campaign to extract a model’s capabilities and replicate them in another model without authorization.” Anthropic said its older models, such as Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4.5, from 2025, “were well below the threshold where they could meaningfully assist a sophisticated user in carrying out dangerous biological research.” “As a result, safeguards on these models were less stringent, directed mostly at preventing access to content that might uplift novices in recreating known bioweapons,” the report said. “But for today’s models — which are capable of assisting in a range of complex scientific research tasks — the evidence is no longer certain, and we cannot make that same assurance.” Because of this, Anthropic has applied “stronger safeguards that restrict access to a wide range of dual-use biological research queries” in its more recent models, such as Claude Fable 5, the report said. As companies introduce increasingly powerful AI models, experts have called on governments to regulate the technology, rather than relying on the industry to police itself. John Thickstun, an assistant professor of computer science at Cornell University, said it is an uncomfortable position for companies like Anthropic and OpenAI to be in when they are expected to determine what is safe vs. unsafe behavior and make “value judgments at societal scale without any kind of democratic or deliberative oversight.” Report follows a researcher’s dire warning Anthropic also found groups that created hundreds of social media accounts that look like they belong to ordinary people and then posted material amplifying the same political view over the course of a week. The company outlined nine such cases it found, originating in Russia, Iran, Turkey and across the Persian Gulf, South Asia, Africa and Europe. While social media companies can detect influence operations on their platforms once posts are circulating, “we may see it on Claude while the operation is still being built.” Anthropic released this report after one of its researchers, Jacob Coxon, announced he’s resigning amid fears the company and its chief rival OpenAI “are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” Coxon’s post warned that some of his colleagues now believe AI could threaten human life by the end of the decade. But Anthropic said it has blocked each of the malicious activities it identified, used the experience to strengthen safeguards and shared information with government authorities and industry partners. “We hope that the findings in this report will help other developers recognize similar patterns on their own platforms, give governments and civil society a clearer view of how emerging threats take shape, and strengthen collective defenses,” Anthropic said.

headlines.title: BART blames heat, aging equipment for Tuesday meltdowns in Daly City
headlines.description: A BART operations official told the agency’s governing board Thursday that aging power equipment was to blame for Tuesday’s Daly City substation fire, which broke out just as BART engineers were scrambling to deal with a rash of apparent heat-related train-control system meltdowns in the same area. At a briefing of the agency’s governing board, BART Operations Manager Sylvia Lamb said hours before the fire Tuesday night, excessive heat apparently caused an air conditioning system failure at the Daly City Station. The subsequent heat buildup in the station, she said, likely explains a rash of “false occupancy” alarms. The alarms trigger when the control system senses trains bunching up close enough to pose a collision hazard. BART responded by manually switching trains and slowing speeds through the area, causing delays all day. Lamb told the board a portable HVAC system is now cooling the station while repairs are under way. Then, apparently unrelated to the false alarms, circuit breakers tripped at the station that evening. BART staff soon discovered the substation fire, which was also spotted by a driver on nearby Interstate 280. The fire created a massive disruption in Transbay service that lasted several hours. BART 5 hours ago BART Sep 9 BART Sep 8 Crews surveying the system later found a damaged 34.5-kv cable feeding power to the station, she said. The substation is designed to cut the 34.5 kv power to 1,000 volts of direct current. Lamb noted the cable, as well as the substation itself, are original equipment on the system built back in the 1970s. Lamb said the fire was likely caused by insulation failure on a single component of the substation. “This is a very clear failure due to aging electrical equipment, it is very obvious,” she said, adding that the Daly City fire was very similar to a fault-triggered fire at a traction power substation in downtown Oakland in 2024. That station was also slated to be repaired under a bond funded project. Lamb noted that about 50 of BART’s 74 traction-power substations have never been replaced and that the station in Daly City was third on of a list of top five stations for replacement. Overhauling a substation, she said, can cost about $4 million, while replacing one can cost up to $60 million. BART has money to replace one additional substation, she said, so moving up the Daly City work will delay another high priority project. Lamb noted that BART is in the process of replacing HVAC systems but did not tell the board how soon that work will be done.

headlines.title: Police investigating deadly shooting in San Jose
headlines.description: Police are investigating a deadly shooting in San Jose’s Willow Glen neighborhood. The incident was reported at 10:20 p.m. Wednesday in the area of Oak and Palm streets. When officers arrived they found a man suffering from at least one gunshot wound. Police said the victim succumbed to his injuries and was pronounced dead by medics at the scene. The San Jose Police Department’s homicide unit has taken over the investigation, which includes trying to determine the motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting. Wednesday’s incident marked San Jose’s 19th homicide of the year. headlines.title: Residents escape 2-alarm fire at San Jose duplex
headlines.description: Firefighters battled a two-alarm blaze that broke out early Thursday morning at a duplex in San Jose’s Cambrian neighborhood, according to fire officials. The fire started just after 6 a.m. at a duplex in the 2900 block of Union Avenue while residents were home. Within about 10 minutes of the first 911 call, San Jose firefighters arrived, made sure everyone was out of the building and began fighting the fire. As flames began shooting through the roof, firefighters had to leave the home and battle the blaze from outside. All residents were able to get out safely, and no firefighters were injured. Despite homes being close together in the neighborhood, the fire did not spread to any other residences. Utilities at the property were secured, according to the fire department. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Fire officials said it was also too early to determine whether the duplex had working smoke alarms.

headlines.title: 9/11 hero Mark Bingham leaves lasting legacy in rugby
headlines.description: There were so many heroes on September 11, 2001. When terrorists hijacked four commercial planes that day, the passengers and crew on United Flight 93 did not go quietly. They fought back and made the ultimate sacrifice to save thousands. The Bay Area’s Mark Bingham was on that flight. 25 years later, his legacy is celebrated and honored in a sport he loved to play in a community often harassed and overlooked. Jessica Aguirre has the story. The men on the pitch have a lot of gratitude for Mark Bingham, whether they knew him or know of him. His legacy lives on in the Fog Rugby. Founded in 2000, Fog is the first gay and inclusive rugby club on the west coast. Bingham is one of the team’s original members. Dany Samreth played against Bingham on the field. He says, “he’s the human equivalent of a golden retriever, right? You know, happy-go-lucky, that guy who will buy you drinks at the bar, but on the field, tough as nails. He will protect your back.” Bingham protected thousands on September 11, 2001. He was among the passengers on the Flight 93 who hatched up a plan to storm the cockpit and overtake the hijackers. They never made it in. The hijackers plummeted the plane into a rural field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Bingham is a national hero for his actions, but it was his bravery every day in life that made him a respected teammate. “It was just meaningful for him to join a team that was focused primarily towards gay and queer men,” says Samreth. Bingham was an avid advocate for the LGBTQ+ community. His name now lives forever in the “Bingham Cup”, the largest amateur rugby tournament in the world. At the Witter Rugby field at UC Berkeley, Bingham is honored every 9/11. He played at Cal and was a member of the university’s 1991 National Championship team. Jack Clark coached Bingham. “We had a reunion in the late spring, you know, before 9-11 and it was a reunion of the 1991 championship team and Mark had come back,” says Clark. He goes on to say, “he was happy and I know that he enjoyed catching up with a lot of his teammates and it was just a short period of time after that that we lost him. We were as much in awe of his sacrifice as anyone and we were proud of Mark.” An etching of Bingham’s name from the National 9/11 memorial and museum in New York hangs at Cal’s Rugby fieldhouse. And, on every September 11, Cal’s rugby squad members do a team run in Mark’s name. Coach Clark says, “we just you know try to make sure that these players understand what happened on 9/11 and its connection to our university and our team.”
headlines.source: Christine Ni, Jessica Aguirre and Robbie Beasom

headlines.title: BART service resumes between San Bruno, Colma; some disruptions remain
headlines.description: BART train service resumed between the San Bruno and Colma stations Thursday morning following the latest in a series of major shutdowns and delays. Riders should expect residual delays in the Antioch, Richmond, SFO Airport and Millbrae directions as service is being restored in the area, BART officials announced at about 9:15 a.m. BART service was halted between the San Francisco International Airport and Colma stations earlier Thursday because of a train control equipment problem near South San Francisco, causing major delays for riders on the Yellow and Red lines. The transit agency issued an alert shortly after 7:10 a.m. about the problem and said riders were directed to shuttle trains that were running between the Millbrae and SFO stations, and between the SFO and San Bruno stations. SamTrans was also providing service on the ECR bus route, with stops between the Millbrae and Colma stations. BART has had ongoing issues in the Peninsula this week after a fire Tuesday night at a traction power substation near the Daly City station. Earlier Thursday, the agency said there was no Green line service to help reduce train congestion between Daly City and Colma.

headlines.title: San Francisco rents jump nearly 25% as mayor declares rent emergency
headlines.description: As a new report shows rents continuing to climb, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie Thursday morning declared a rent emergency that needs to be addressed immediately. San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu also weighed in on the city’s rent prices, saying they are “too damn high.” The numbers back are backing that. New numbers from rental marketplace Zumper show the cost of a two-bedroom apartment in San Francisco has increased 24.6% compared with last year, with monthly rent now topping $6,100. San Francisco isn’t the only Bay Area city seeing higher rents, with San Jose and Oakland also seeing jumps from last year. At a news conference Thursday morning, Lurie and local leaders unveiled a sweeping package of a half dozen reforms, including protections from unfair evictions for renters and new rules to protect against sudden jumps in rent. City Attorney Chiu talked about enforcement of policies. “Tenant protection laws can only help if tenants know about them and they are enforced,” Chiu added. The mayor’s proposal comes as San Francisco continues to see a booming of AI companies and high paid AI workers moving into a city that already has a housing shortage, which is pushing up rent and pushing out the middle class, including teachers, nurses and artists. City leaders said a “full pandemic recovery” can’t happen without proposals. “And as elected leaders in this city, we need to take action that meets the moment,” Lurie said.
headlines.source: Ginger Conejero Saab and Christie Smith

headlines.title: At least 10 Pleasanton businesses hit in string of break-ins
headlines.description: At least 10 businesses were targeted in a series of smash-and-grab break-ins early Thursday morning in Pleasanton. NBC Bay Area witnessed three of the break-ins at businesses near Santa Rita Road at about 4:30 a.m. An NBC Bay Area photographer spotted a group of about four or five people dressed in black smashing the front glass doors of businesses before leaving in a silver vehicle. NBC Bay Area called 911, and three Pleasanton police units arrived within minutes. Officers attempted to box in the vehicle, but the suspects drove away, leading police on a brief pursuit. The vehicle traveled down Valley Avenue and onto Stanley Boulevard with its lights off. Police eventually called off the pursuit near Isabel Avenue because of concerns for public safety. Police were already searching for suspects following reports of break-ins at about 3:50 a.m. at several businesses at Pacific Pearl shopping center near the Livermore outlets. Surveillance video provided to NBC Bay Area by the owner of a Korean fried chicken restaurant showed people smashing their way into the business and leaving within seconds with cash. Six restaurants at Pacific Pearl and four businesses near Santa Rita Road appeared to have been targeted, including two restaurants, a nail salon and Perry’s Liquors. Cash was taken from registers in several of the break-ins. No arrests had been reported as of Thursday morning.
